claims.text: The starting protective coating contains both FCC and BCC phases.
Standard deposition produces a fine-scale interpenetrating FCC/BCC microstructure.
The starting coating has a typical but nonoptimized fraction of coherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
Tailored post-deposition annealing or adjusted deposition parameters can increase the fraction and quality of coherent FCC/BCC interphase boundaries.
The modified processing route will produce coatings with greater interphase coherence than standard processing.
Coherent FCC/BCC interphase boundaries impede dislocation movement under sustained loading.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces act as strong dislocation-pinning sites.
Impeded dislocation motion slows plastic-deformation rate and reduces creep-strain accumulation.
At identical stress and temperature, the coating with enhanced coherent interfaces will accumulate significantly less creep strain than the standard coating.
The beneficial behavior is expected when dislocation-based and diffusive creep mechanisms are active under moderate-to-high temperature and sustained load.
The predicted benefit is not expected when catastrophic microstructural degradation dominates.
Significant microstructural coarsening or phase instability would fall outside the intended operating regime.
Creep resistance may depend on microstructural evolution during testing.
The temperature and stress limits for retaining beneficial interface coherence are not known precisely.
